# Recall goes through the workspace, lookup goes around it

*A controlled test of the J++ lens on two-step questions in open models: what it reads at the middle entity, and whether the model uses it.*

**Zach Perlman and Danyil Orel** · MATS 12.0 sprint, Neel Nanda's stream · 19–30 Oct 2026<!-- src: docs/plans/hypotheses.md | The proposal (19 Oct) --><!-- src: docs/depth/README.md | 29 Oct 2026 -->

## TL;DR

Gurnee et al. (2026) argue that the J++ lens reads a "workspace" holding the middle step of a model's reasoning. We tested this on two-step questions that pass through a middle entity, the *bridge*. Their second step is *recalled* from memory or *looked up* in the prompt. A *knock-out* removes the *lens part*, the few directions the lens reads most at the bridge, over a band of middle layers.

- **Recall needs the lens directions at the bridge; lookup needs far less.** The knock-out costs recalled answers 42.6<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | ko.q9.mk --> to 53.1<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | ko.nl.mk --> points more than looked-up ones on Qwen 9B, Qwen 27B and Lightning, the three clearest of nine models.
- **The lookup goes around the lens.** It finds the item by its identity or by an address, a code for where the item sits in the prompt. A probe reads the address at 0.85 to 0.99<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv | the locker probe at the bridge word, locker-first scenes -->, and swapping it in redirects the lookup; the lens directions do not capture it.
- **Neither the knock-out nor the readout shows that a step is used.** The knock-out mostly removes the answer's own directions. At the answer position a probe on the lens part reads the entity at 0.91 to 0.98, yet swapping that part moves at most 0.14 ○ of answers<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv | 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the probe's accuracy on the lens part; 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the lens swap's switches -->.
- **For monitoring.** At an entity, a lens readout shows which entity is in play and what it brings to mind. It does not show whether the model answers from memory or from the text.

![Taking the lens part out breaks recalled answers, not lookup ones](figures/readme/02_main_split.png)

*Removing the lens part costs recall far more than lookup, in both tests. Each row joins a model's lookup to its recall, with the gap at the right. Left: the knock-out over a band of layers (fact passages), answers turned wrong, in points. Right: removal from the patch at one layer (locker scenes), switches blocked beyond a random part.*

## Setup

Take one scene: "The locker of carbon is 3. The locker of helium is 5. … Eric picked **carbon**."<!-- src: docs/depth/README.md | The locker of carbon is 3. The locker of helium is 5. --> Asked which locker belongs to Eric's pick, the model looks up 3 in the text<!-- src: docs/depth/README.md | Which locker belongs to Eric's pick?" (3, found in the prompt) -->. Asked the atomic number of Eric's pick, it recalls 6 from memory<!-- src: docs/depth/README.md | What is the atomic number of Eric's pick?" (6, from memory) -->. Both questions pass through the bridge, *carbon*. The fact passages pose the same contrast with real facts, giving the bridge's fact or leaving it to memory. Five models are tested on locker scenes, nine on fact passages.

Real items, each picked by a fixed rule (rules and item ids in `data/figures/examples/data.csv`). The fact passage is chosen to show the typical flip, and its caption says how often that flip occurs.

![One real locker scene, Qwen 27B: the whole change switches both readers; without the lens part the lookup still switches and the recall does not](figures/examples/01_locker_scene.png)

*Without the lens part the lookup still switches and the recall does not. One locker scene, Qwen 27B (the bridge word in bold): each reader's answer before the change and under each operation at layer 32<!-- src: docs/depth/x0_numbers.json | layer_27b -->. Over the main test's 200<!-- src: docs/depth/x0_numbers.json | n_27b --> scenes, the recall switches without the lens part in only 35<!-- src: docs/depth/x0_numbers.json | rc_noj_27b -->.*

### Key terms

- **Bridge.** The entity a two-step question passes through. **Recall** and **lookup** answer its second step from memory and from the prompt.
- **Lens part.** The few directions the J++ lens reads most at the bridge. The **logit lens**, read through the output layer, is a control.
- **Knock-out.** The lens part removed at every token over a band of middle layers.
- **Patch.** The change between two prompts' states at the bridge word and one layer. An answer **switches** when the patch makes it the other prompt's answer. **Remove from the patch** adds the patch back without its lens part.
- **Swap.** Another entity's lens part written into the bridge. A **probe** is a linear classifier on hidden states.
- **Identity and address.** Which item the bridge is, and where its sentence sits in the prompt.
- **Answer span.** The answers' own lens directions.
- **Post hoc (○).** A gate or rule set after the data were seen. More in the [glossary](docs/shared/glossary_joint.md).

![Three tools, one target: the lens part at the bridge.](figures/readme/01_tools.png)

*Three tests of the lens part at the bridge, drawn over the first example's last words (rows are layers, columns tokens; teal marks the cells changed). The knock-out removes it at every token over a band of layers. Removal from the patch adds the patch back without it. The swap writes in another entity's.*

### Reading the figures

Each colour is a role. Recall is black, lookup violet, the lens part teal, the address amber, identity blue, a gap slate, and a control grey. Hollow marks (○) are post hoc; whiskers are 95% intervals over bridge items<!-- src: docs/breadth/README.md | Brackets: 95% bootstrap over bridges -->. Fact passages count in points, locker scenes in shares.

## Findings

### Finding 1. Recall needs the lens part; lookup needs far less

The knock-out breaks recalled answers and leaves looked-up ones nearly intact. On Qwen 9B, Qwen 27B and Lightning the recall drops 42.6<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | ko.q9.mk --> to 53.1<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | ko.nl.mk --> points more than the lookup. Same-size controls cost far less. At one layer the recall follows the lens part when the patch's parts disagree, and the lookup does not. On the other six models the split is weaker or not specific ([Where it does not hold](#where-it-does-not-hold)).

![Random, rotated, logit-lens and PCA directions cost far less than the lens part](figures/readme/03_controls.png)

*Same-size controls cost far less than the lens part. Left: the recall − lookup gap when the knock-out removes the lens part (teal) or a same-size control (grey: a rotated part, the logit lens's or the top principal directions). Right: the lens part minus its largest control, paired on the same items.*

### Finding 2. The lookup goes around the lens, through an identity or an address

When another item moves, the lookup follows either the item's own locker (its identity) or the position its locker sat in (the address). It never follows the new number. A probe at the bridge word reads the address at 0.85 to 0.99<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv | the locker probe at the bridge word, locker-first scenes -->. Removing the address from the patch stops lookups by position; swapping in another locker's address redirects the lookup. The lens directions rebuild almost none of that swap, so a lens monitor misses both codes.

![One real routes scene, Qwen 9B: the three routes predict three lockers; the lookup takes the identity route's](figures/examples/03_routes.png)

*The three routes predict three different lockers, and here the lookup takes the identity route's. One scene, Qwen 9B, in which another item moved. Over such scenes the whole change sends the lookup to the identity route's locker in 0.48<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv | another item moved, whole: identity share --> of them.*

![A swap of the address moves the lookup; the lens misses it](figures/readme/07_address_swap_lens.png)

*Swapping in another locker's address moves the lookup, and the lens directions do not rebuild that swap. Left: lookups sent to the new locker (amber), against a same-size random vector (grey). Right: how far above random vectors the lens rebuilds the swap (amber), against a same-size change of item (blue, the positive control).*

<details><summary>Test, results, controls and limits</summary>

- **Test.** Train a probe at the bridge word to read which locker sentence holds the item's locker. Remove the probe's directions from the patch. Write another locker's address in. Measure how much of that write the lens directions rebuild.
- **Result.** Shares of the lookup's answers; Lightning is post hoc throughout.

- **Controls.** A probe trained on the layout only reads the address at 0.53<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv | the locker probe's layout baseline, locker-first scenes -->. A random vector sends at most 0.01 of lookups anywhere<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv | lookup target share, random direction, s = 4 -->. The 25 lens directions rebuild 0.01 to 0.06 of the address swap<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv | 47.0 (b) share rebuilt by 25 lens directions: pointer -->, as little as for a random vector.
- **Scope.** The identity code lies outside the lens on the 9B, 27B, Muse and Lightning; the 122B was below its gate. The address was found in the locker scenes:
  - removing it cuts position answers beyond a random part on five models, and a swap moves lookups to the swapped-in locker, also across neutral sentences;
  - on the varied scenes (prose, JSON, tables) the address fit on simple scenes does little, but refit on each format it carries the lookup again on the 9B, Muse and Lightning, not the 27B;
  - on the fact passages the lookup rarely takes the position route the address serves (almost never on the 27B), and the natural passages were not tested;
  - in Python code and tool output (exploratory, the 9B and the 27B) it is readable and needed, added alone it brings few position answers back, and the swap was not run there.
- **Confidence.** Credence [~80%](docs/plans/credences.md)<!-- src: docs/plans/credences.md | address -->. The swap's dose was chosen after its rule, fixed in advance, was read at the wrong dose and said no on every model<!-- src: docs/depth/README.md | read at s = 1 and said no on every model -->.
- **Limits.** The 27B's address is weak, and adding it alone does not bring position answers back. The probe is refit for each format. Which code each lookup gives up, scene by scene, is post hoc ([figure](figures/readme/10_two_codes.png)). The address points to the item's mention, not to a number; on the 9B and Lightning its swap also changes some recalls ([depth report](docs/depth/README.md#part-iii-the-address-where-the-items-locker-sits)).

### Finding 3. Neither the knock-out nor the readout shows that a step is used

#### Removing

The knock-out's damage to recall is the answer's own directions. Removing only the answer span does all of it, in a test fixed in advance on three models. Keeping the answer span undoes 0.91<!-- src: data/figures/writeup/data.csv | fig10.keep_span.nl --> to 0.95<!-- src: data/figures/writeup/data.csv | fig10.keep_span.q27 --> of it. So the knock-out shows that recall needs the directions of its remembered word, not that the bridge is used. The claims about the bridge rest on the one-layer test (Finding 1) and the swap (below).

![Keeping only the answer span's directions undoes nearly all of the recall's damage; removing only them does all of it](figures/writeup/10_answer_span.png)

*What the knock-out removes from the recall is its answer's own directions. Left: the share of the damage undone when the answer span is kept (brick), against an energy-matched random keep (grey); descriptive. Middle: the damage when only the answer span is removed, as a multiple of the full knock-out's. Right: the same on the codename set.*

<details><summary>Removing: test, results and limits</summary>

- **Test.** On the twin set, the knock-out keeping the answer span's directions, and the answer span removed alone, each net of a random part of the same energy. On a one-hop question about the subject (a city), removing its lens directions, the answer span, or its directions made orthogonal to the answers. A subspace built from the data and cleaned of the answers, against the rule fixed in advance: under 15 points beyond random means the subject is not seen<!-- src: data/figures/writeup/data.csv | fig11.clean_subspace.q27 -->.
- **Result.**

- **Read.** The keep is descriptive; the answer-only removal was fixed in advance. The orthogonal arm is post hoc on all three models and has no interval. All three subspace estimates are under the bar, but the 27B's and Lightning's intervals reach above it, so that test is not decisive there.
- **Confidence.** Credence [~85%](docs/plans/credences.md)<!-- src: docs/plans/credences.md | answer_directions --> that the damage is the answer's own directions, [~55%](docs/plans/credences.md)<!-- src: docs/plans/credences.md | beyond_countries --> that this holds beyond the countries relation, [~65%](docs/plans/credences.md)<!-- src: docs/plans/credences.md | orthogonal --> that answer-orthogonal removals cannot see the subject.

#### Reading

At the bridge the lens part works as a reference to the entity: what its words evoke. Swapped into another prompt it redirects the recall, even from one neutral sentence naming the entity. At the answer position a probe on the lens part reads the entity at 0.91 to 0.98<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv | 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the probe's accuracy on the lens part -->. Swapping that part moves at most 0.14 ○ of the answers<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv | 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the lens swap's switches -->. A readout at an entity reports what it brings to mind, not what the model uses.

<details><summary>Reading: test, results and limits</summary>

- **Test.** Swap another entity's lens part into the bridge, taken from its own passage or from one neutral sentence naming it. At the last token, train a probe on the lens part to read the recall's entity, then swap only the lens part and compare with patching the whole state.
- **Result at the bridge**, points of answers moved to the other entity's fact.

| | 9B | 27B | Lightning |
|---|---|---|---|
| the lens part from the entity's own passage | 63.9<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv \| swap.q9.swap --> | 63.0<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv \| swap.q27.swap --> | 44.8<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv \| swap.nl.swap --> |
| from one neutral sentence, as a multiple of the above | 1.10<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv \| ptr.q9.neutral --> | 1.09<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv \| ptr.q27.neutral --> | 1.01<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv \| ptr.nl.neutral --> |
| control: a probe's subspace that reads the fact | 5.5<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv \| probe.q9.probe --> | 8.3<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv \| probe.q27.probe --> | 2.2<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv \| probe.nl.probe --> |
| the lens part on the same relations | 79.5<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv \| probe.q9.swap --> | 74.8<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv \| probe.q27.swap --> | 62.4<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv \| probe.nl.swap --> |

- **Result at the answer position**, shares of recalls; Lightning is post hoc.

| | 9B | 27B | Muse | Lightning | 122B |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| probe on the lens part reads the entity | 0.97<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the probe's accuracy on the lens part --> | 0.95<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the probe's accuracy on the lens part --> | 0.95<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the probe's accuracy on the lens part --> | 0.98<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the probe's accuracy on the lens part --> ○ | 0.91<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the probe's accuracy on the lens part --> |
| recalls switched by swapping the lens part | 0.00<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the lens swap's switches --> | 0.01<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the lens swap's switches --> | 0.01<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the lens swap's switches --> | 0.14<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the lens swap's switches --> ○ | 0.00<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the lens swap's switches --> |
| … by patching the whole state | 0.95<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the whole-state patch's switches --> | 0.97<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the whole-state patch's switches --> | 1.00<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the whole-state patch's switches --> | 0.97<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the whole-state patch's switches --> ○ | 0.79<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv \| 51.10: recall, last token, read peak: the whole-state patch's switches --> |

- **More.** In the locker scenes the lens part is the old and the new bridge words, almost never the answer word. Across nine models the entity is readable everywhere and needed only in some: OLMo 32B carries it (swap 41.4) without needing it (knock-out 5.4)<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | swap.ol.swap; ko.ol.mk --> ([nine models](figures/readme/13_nine_models.png)). In a conflict between memory and the passage (twin set), the bridge shows the remembered attribute about as strongly whichever source wins.
- **Scope.** The neutral-sentence reference holds on 8 of 8 relations on the 27B<!-- src: docs/breadth/README.md | It holds on 8 of 8 relations on the 27B -->. It needs words that name the entity: a codename defined in the passage shows almost nothing of the person.
- **Confidence.** Credence [~70%](docs/plans/credences.md)<!-- src: docs/plans/credences.md | associations --> that the bridge shows what its words evoke, [~50%](docs/plans/credences.md)<!-- src: docs/plans/credences.md | swap_through_answer --> that the swap runs through the answer on our items, [~80%](docs/plans/credences.md)<!-- src: docs/plans/credences.md | readable_not_used --> that readable is not always used.
- **Limits.** "Not used" means not used at that token and layer, at a real change's size; at twice that size the lens part moves part of Muse's and Lightning's recalls. At described bridges the swap's effect runs through the answer's directions.

![Another entity's lens part moves the recall from any context, a probe's subspace that reads the fact does not](figures/readme/04_pointer.png)

*Another entity's lens part moves the recall to that entity's fact, even from one neutral sentence; a probe's subspace that reads the fact barely does. Rows: the source of the part swapped in at the bridge. Dots: answers moved, in points.*

## What we predicted, and what happened

Our committed guesses and their verdicts; the sources are in the [hypotheses ledger](docs/plans/hypotheses.md).

- The bridge counts only through its own word → **failed** for recalled entities, **held in part** for computed numbers ([ledger row](docs/plans/hypotheses.md#h0-deflationary-failed-for-recalled-entities-held-in-part-for-computed-numbers)).
- A bridge used to recall is inside, one used to look up is outside → **not separable** from the next guess ([ledger row](docs/plans/hypotheses.md#h1-use-not-separable-from-h2-on-the-main-tests-where-they-come-apart-the-data-follow-h2)).
- A recalled answer keeps the bridge inside → **favored, not proven** ([ledger row](docs/plans/hypotheses.md#h2-answer-source-favored-not-proven)).
- Any lookup in the chain puts the bridge outside → **failed** ([ledger row](docs/plans/hypotheses.md#h3-any-retrieval-from-context-failed)).
- Memory steps need the lens part, prompt lookups do not → **held**, graded across models ([ledger row](docs/plans/hypotheses.md#c1-memory-steps-need-the-j-space-prompt-lookups-dont-held-graded-across-models)).
- The lens steers recall-used bridges, not lookup-used ones → **withdrawn**, replaced by the swap ([ledger row](docs/plans/hypotheses.md#c2-reading--using-the-lens-steers-recall-used-bridges-not-lookup-used-ones-withdrawn-24-oct)).
- A bridge in the prompt is written only when a recall uses it → **held in part** ([ledger row](docs/plans/hypotheses.md#c2-a-stated-or-computed-bridge-is-written-only-when-a-recall-uses-it-held-in-part)).
- Computed bridges sit in the workspace → **not tested in the final design** ([ledger row](docs/plans/hypotheses.md#c3-computed-bridges-sit-in-the-j-space-beyond-their-own-word-not-tested-in-the-final-design)).
- The split follows the Olmo architecture → **failed** ([ledger row](docs/plans/hypotheses.md#architecture-22-oct-c1-holds-on-olmo-hybrid-7b-and-fails-on-olmo-3-7b-failed)).
- Muse's recalls survive the knock-out → **did not reproduce** on the main passage set ([ledger row](docs/plans/hypotheses.md#the-muse-puzzle-22-oct-removal-barely-touches-muses-recalls-while-writing-redirects-them-did-not-reproduce-on-jsuite-v2)).
- An address readout steers the lookup → **held in part** ([ledger row](docs/plans/hypotheses.md#a-pointer-readout-that-steers-the-lookup-depth-held-in-part)).
- Gemma and the Olmo post-training ladder → **not tested** ([Gemma](docs/plans/hypotheses.md#gemma-4-31b-not-tested-in-the-final-design-untestable), [ladder](docs/plans/hypotheses.md#the-olmo-3-7b-post-training-ladder-base-sft-dpo-instruct-not-tested-in-the-final-design)).

## Where it does not hold

- **Longer chains.** On three-hop chains the cost does not simply follow the recalled hop. Lightning fits that rule; the 27B breaks it twice, once dropping only 8.2<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | mod.q27.threehop.paper10.PPM-PPP --> points.
- **The 27B's lookup** leans on the lens part partly: 0.60<!-- src: docs/depth/x0_numbers.json | lk_excess_k100_27b --> of its switches are blocked beyond random at 100 directions.
- **Known facts.** When the passage gives a fact the model knows, the 9B's and 27B's lookups follow the lens part (0.26 to 0.28 beyond random)<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv | Z1: lookup, switches lost beyond a random part -->.
- **Across models the split is graded.** It is strong and specific on three of nine. On the rest it is weaker, not specific, shared with the logit lens, or gone when scored by probability.
- **Two tests disagree on two models.** The 122B fails the band test by probability but passes the one-layer test. Muse shares much of its band effect with the logit lens, but not at one layer.

<details><summary>Chains, order and model by model</summary>

- **Chains.** Each hop is read in the passage (P) or recalled (M); the rule says a chain needs the lens part when its last hop is recalled. On the 27B, P → P → M costs 8.2 [-4, 21]<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | mod.q27.threehop.paper10.PPM-PPP --> points beyond the all-passage chain, on the second seed 8.6 [-4, 23]<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | mod2.q27.threehop.paper10.PPM-PPP -->. M → M → P costs 20.5 [5, 35]<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | mod.q27.threehop.paper10.MMP-PPP -->, which was not predicted. The 9B's chains cannot be read: its all-passage chain alone drops 45.8<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | mod.q9.threehop.paper10.loss.PPP --> points ([chain figures](figures/breadth/10a1_beyond.png)).

  ![One real entity, Qwen 27B: only the chain that ends in two recalls turns wrong, and only without the lens part](figures/examples/04_chains.png)

  *On this entity only the chain ending in two recalls turns wrong, and only without the lens part. Three three-hop chains, Qwen 27B: each hop is read in the passage (P) or recalled (M). Answers before the removal, with the lens part removed, and with a rotated part removed.*

- **The 27B's lookup** at 25 directions: 0.14<!-- src: docs/depth/x0_numbers.json | lk_excess_27b --> beyond random; the 122B's at 100 directions: −0.12<!-- src: docs/depth/x0_numbers.json | lk_excess_k100_122b --> ([figure](figures/readme/14_directions.png)).
- **Question order** has no general effect. With the question before the scene, the 27B's lookup has 0.11<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv | the lookup, question before minus after (paired) --> more of its switches blocked (interval from 0.01<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv | 53.1: the lookup, question before minus after (paired): the interval's lower bound -->); the 122B's -0.05<!-- src: data/figures/depth/data.csv | the lookup, question before minus after (paired) -->. On the twin set the 27B's lookup leans less on it, and the 9B's and Lightning's do not move.
- **Known facts.** With made-up facts the split returns on the 9B and the 122B.
- **Model by model.** Weak: Ministral 23.3 and DeepSeek 17.9 points<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | ko.mi.mk; ko.ds.mk -->. Not specific on Bolt and DeepSeek: at 100 directions a same-size principal-direction removal costs 24.0 against 31.3, and 25.9 against 28.7<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | dose.nb.k100.pc; dose.nb.k100; dose.ds.k100.pc; dose.ds.k100 -->. Shared with the logit lens: Muse, 34.6 of its 59.9<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | ko.mu.u; ko.mu.mk -->. Gone by probability: the 122B's 48.5 drops to 1.7<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | ko.q122.mk; ko.q122.soft -->. Untestable: the knock-out breaks plain text on Gemma 4 31B-it, gpt-oss-20b and Kolibri-1 (9.3, 4.7 and 6.4 nats added)<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | text.gemma; text.gptoss; text.kol -->.
- **Agents.** On one relation posed as agent tasks, the knock-out costs producing the answer 35.7<!-- src: data/figures/writeup/data.csv | figA1.produce.q9 --> / 36.6<!-- src: data/figures/writeup/data.csv | figA1.produce.q27 --> / 50.8<!-- src: data/figures/writeup/data.csv | figA1.produce.nl --> points beyond a rotated part, picking the true one of two 10.1<!-- src: data/figures/writeup/data.csv | figA1.pick.q9 --> / 4.5<!-- src: data/figures/writeup/data.csv | figA1.pick.q27 --> / 2.3<!-- src: data/figures/writeup/data.csv | figA1.pick.nl -->, and verifying a claim −16.3<!-- src: data/figures/writeup/data.csv | figA1.verify.q9 --> / 3.8<!-- src: data/figures/writeup/data.csv | figA1.verify.q27 --> / 3.7<!-- src: data/figures/writeup/data.csv | figA1.verify.nl --> (9B / 27B / Lightning; several cells descriptive; [figure](figures/writeup/a01_agents.png)). Credence [~55%](docs/plans/credences.md)<!-- src: docs/plans/credences.md | agents -->.
- **Pretraining.** The 9B base model's split is 33.7<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | v1.q9base.qa -->, its instruct model's 41.2<!-- src: docs/breadth/data.csv | v1.q9inst.qa -->.

</details>

## How we checked

- **Rules fixed in advance.** Breadth runs follow a [pre-registration](docs/breadth/prereg_replication_1022.md) with amendments committed before each run. Depth [predictions](predictions/README.md) were committed before results were opened, then scored; they did worse than always guessing even odds (mean Brier 0.32)<!-- src: docs/depth/README.md | mean Brier 0.32 over 121 answers -->.
- **Reruns.** From a clean checkout the breadth headline runs match row for row: 0 of 22325 rows differ on the 27B<!-- src: docs/breadth/README.md | 0 of 22325 -->.
- **Independent recounts.** Code written from scratch recounts the depth headline numbers and matches 63 of 63<!-- src: docs/depth/README.md | matches 63 of 63 -->.
- **What we dropped**, with the test that dropped it: [depth](docs/depth/README.md#tested-and-dropped), [breadth](docs/breadth/README.md#8-what-did-not-hold).

<details><summary>Run provenance and red-teaming</summary>

- **The runs behind this page.** Its numbers trace to 102<!-- src: data/figures/provenance.csv | prov.runs --> run folders: 5<!-- src: data/figures/provenance.csv | prov.no_commit --> of their manifests record no git commit, and 22<!-- src: data/figures/provenance.csv | prov.no_lens_sha --> no lens sha256 (where a commit is recorded, the lens follows from the model's pin at that commit, `configs/models/*.yaml`); 24<!-- src: data/figures/provenance.csv | prov.untraced --> cited files are CPU read-outs or verdicts with no manifest of their own. Counted by `scripts/provenance_counts.py`.
- **Environment switches.** The 43<!-- src: data/figures/provenance.csv | g1.writers_unrecorded --> late-sprint run scripts did not record their environment switches; 26<!-- src: data/figures/provenance.csv | g1.writers_switches --> of them now do, and the other 17<!-- src: data/figures/provenance.csv | g1.writers_left_out --> load no model. For the runs already on disk the `BJ_` variables (device map, batch size) were not recorded.
- **Depth reruns and checks.** Rerun labels agree on 382-400 of 400 items per arm<!-- src: docs/depth/README.md | 382-400 of 400 items per arm -->; automatic checks read 45,942 items<!-- src: docs/depth/README.md | 45,942 items read --> and their recount matches 245 of 245 numbers<!-- src: docs/depth/README.md | their recount matches 245 of 245 -->.
- **Red-teaming.** A shortcut in one twin-set variant, and false values in the conflict variant that were too easy to reject, were fixed by rebuilding both sets before any result was read.

</details>

## Related work and what is new

- **Not new.** Removing the top lens directions hurts free-form recall and multi-step reasoning (Gurnee et al. 2026<!-- src: docs/shared/references.md | Gurnee et al. 2026 -->). Subjects are enriched with their attributes (Geva et al. 2023<!-- src: docs/shared/references.md | Geva, Bastings, Filippova and Globerson 2023 -->). Entities are bound in context (Feng & Steinhardt 2023) and found through "lookback pointers", our addresses (Prakash et al. 2025)<!-- src: docs/depth/README.md | (Feng & Steinhardt 2023); "lookback pointers" [addresses] (Prakash et al. 2025) -->. Memory and context are arbitrated outside the verbal workspace (Kawada & Kellis 2026<!-- src: docs/shared/references.md | Kawada and Kellis 2026 -->).
- **New here.** Matched recall and lookup twins across nine models with three kinds of control. The address as the part the lens misses (where it holds: [Finding 2](#finding-2-the-lookup-goes-around-the-lens-through-an-identity-or-an-address), Scope). False positives and negatives of lens readouts at entities.
- **Methods we build on.** Gur-Arieh et al. (2025) for the routes, mass-mean directions (Marks & Tegmark 2023) for the address, Makelov et al. (2023) for random parts<!-- src: docs/depth/README.md | Gur-Arieh et al. (2025); (Marks & Tegmark 2023); Makelov et al. (2023) -->. All [references](docs/shared/references.md).

## Open questions

<details><summary>Seven open questions, each with what we would run next</summary>

- **Why does the 27B behave differently?** Next, the same twin items through both lookup measures.
- **Why does the recall follow the lens part without needing it at one layer?** Removing it over four layers costs the 9B's recall about a quarter<!-- src: docs/depth/README.md | Removing it over four layers costs the 9B's recall about a quarter. -->. Next, map where the other copies sit.
- **Does the address exist in natural text?** Next, a probe trained on one format and tested on another.
- **Can a monitor tell recall from lookup?** Next, a lens readout plus an address probe, scored on which source the model uses.
- **Does a computed bridge go through the workspace?** Computed numbers do not; a computed entity is untested.
- **What makes models differ?** Next, OLMo through the dose grid, and base and instruct pairs of one family.
- **Beyond our setting.** Next, multi-token answers and reasoning traces.

</details>
